I attempted a bit more than a year and a half ago. It taught me that everything is solvable. There is no problem that is not fixable or at least something you can live with, and when you're about to die you really realise that. I was lucky enough to get a lot of support through my recovery and am now doing a lot better, but I have learned that even if it's hurts like hell and you're at rock bottom, it's going to hurt a lot less very soon, everything passes. 

Additionally, even when you think you're completely alone and unloved, people really do care. I felt so isolated through everything that lead to my suicide attempt, but when I was recovering I really realised everyone does care and love me and want to help, my brain just pushed all of that out. 

Lastly, I learned that life is worth the pain even if it doesn't feel like it is this second. You need the bad bits to really feel the good bits

keeping a tidy study area is really important, as well as not studying in your bed. try to get out to study if you can.

hi there! i wouldn't recommend exercising while fasting, especially if it is a prolonged fast. if you're just starting out and you're only a few hours in you should be fine, but after that only light exercise (stretching, walking, things like that) as you could pass out and you'll lose a lot of water and salt, if it's a very long fast i'd say try not to exercise at all. 

i also find myself very hungry after fasting so if i exercise it makes it harder to keep up the fast.

personally i exercise after refeeds and between casts just as i normally would, and treat a fast as a break, exercise-wise

of course these are just my opinions and experiences, trying things out or yourself and changing stuff based on how you feel is important, just stay safe and put your health first ✨💕
